Summary  
The provided Alignment Newsletter excerpt discusses several AI safety‐relevant research results: (1) certified adversarial robustness for deep RL, (2) assistance via empowerment instead of goal inference, (3) automatic reward-machine discovery for POMDPs, (4) proprioception-augmented imitation-from-observation, and (5) theoretical analysis of convergent instrumental subgoals and policy quantilization.  
The knowledge fabric below links five top-level risks to these research lines through problem analyses, theoretical insights, design rationales, implementation mechanisms, validation evidence and finally to actionable interventions, while re-using common nodes (e.g. “Partial observability of environmental state in high-dimensional tasks”) to ensure one connected graph.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[83] – I am reasonably confident the core causal-interventional pathways and node/edge metadata are correct and the JSON is syntactically valid. Remaining uncertainty stems from the newsletter’s informal prose and limited methodological detail.

Inference strategy justification  
• Light inference (confidence 2) was used only where the newsletter gives qualitative statements (e.g. assuming partial-observability causes adversarial vulnerability) or purely theoretical proposals (quantilizers).  
• No speculative interventions were invented beyond what a safety researcher would naturally draw from each paper.

Extraction completeness explanation  
All explicit reasoning chains in the text that reach an actionable method were captured, decomposed into ~30 concept nodes and 5 intervention nodes (≈15 nodes / 5 000 words). Paths are cross-connected through shared causes (partial observability) and shared theory (goal locality), satisfying the “fabric” criterion.

Key limitations  
• The newsletter summarises rather than fully specifies methods; descriptions may omit implementation minutiae.  
• Some validation evidence is qualitative, lowering edge confidence.  
• Quantilizer safety lacks empirical validation; a theoretical evidence node was used instead.
